newsitem.title: USA: More than 37 million visit Orlando in 1996 -- report.
newsitem.headline: More than 37 million visit Orlando in 1996 -- report.

text.p: More than 37 million Americans visited Orlando for pleasure or business in 1996, a rise of 11.7 per cent over 1995, figures released on Friday said.
Leisure visitors totaled 29.5 million, up 10.5 per cent, the Orlando/Orange County Convention and Visitors Bureau said in a statement.
Of these 13.8 million were Florida residents and the rest from elsewhere in the United States.

The number of business travelers increased 16.6 per cent to 7.6 million. Floridians accounted for 4.4 million of these, up 20 per cent, while out-of-state business travelers rose 12.5 per cent to 3.2 million.

"When Orlando racks up double digit percentage increases in every category of domestic visitor counts in one year it speaks volumes about what a great leisure and business destination the area has become," Bureau Director William Pepper said in the statement.
He said more visitors were expected in the future as new hotels and theme park attractions were due to open in 1998.
Most out-of-state visitors came as families and stayed an average of 5.5 days. The main activity of 87 per cent was to visit theme parks.
Of Florida visitors, 37 per cent came as couples followed by 29 per cent who came as families. They mostly stayed 1.6 days and visiting theme parks was again the main activity.
The top 10 states of origin for visitor's were New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Michigan, Georgia, New Jersey, Texas, Illinois, North Carolina and Indiana. ((--U.S. Municipal Desk, 212-859-1650))
